name: performance-testing
description: Performance testing — JMeter load plans, thresholds, CI-safe execution
body:
# Performance Testing

Apply when editing JMeter plans, performance runners, or `qa.config.json` jmeter section.

## Source of truth

- Configure load in **`qa.config.json`** → `jmeter` (threads, ramp-up, loop count, path).
- Run **`npm run qa:sync`** to update `tests/performance/load-test.jmx`.
- Prefer editing config + sync over manual JMX-only changes.

## Performance considerations

Before raising load, assess:

- **Target environment** — never load-test production without explicit approval.
- **Thread count & ramp-up** — start conservative; increase incrementally.
- **Assertions** — response code, response time thresholds, error rate limits.
- **Side effects** — read-heavy vs write-heavy endpoints; auth/session impact on shared envs.

Document expected baseline (threads, avg response time, error rate) in test comments or `qa.config.json` notes when non-obvious.

## Test types

| Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| **Smoke load** | Small thread count validates endpoint under light concurrency |
| **Regression** | Re-run prior scenario after infra or API changes |
| **Boundary** | Ramp to configured max threads; watch for degradation |

## Execution

```bash
npm run test:performance
```

Reports: `reports/jmeter/results.jtl`, `reports/jmeter/html/index.html`.

## Failure triage

- **Product/infra defect**: sustained high latency, 5xx, timeouts under expected load.
- **Automation defect**: wrong host/path, JMeter not installed, malformed JMX — fix config or runner.
- Never hide failures by removing listeners or assertions to make runs pass.

Keep plans **CI/CD-ready** — non-GUI mode, deterministic paths, no local-only hardcoded directories.
